requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: inventorysvc (uid 992) created since it didn't exist, then /srv/inventory recursively chowned. ls -lanR confirms uid 992 on directory, data/ dir, and both files, both before and after the reboot.

inventory-readers group (gid 1000) created, directories set to 750 and files to 640 (group r-x/r-- retained). Live test with a group-member test user successfully read config.json, and inventorysvc itself could read records.csv, both pre- and post-reboot.

Permissions (750/640) remove all other-bits. Live negative tests: an unrelated outsider-tester user was denied both file read and directory listing pre-reboot, and the 'nobody' user was denied file read post-reboot.

config.json ({"site":"north","generation":4}) and records.csv (sku-1001,keyboard,12 / sku-1002,display,7) content is identical in the pre-change capture, the post-chown/chmod capture, and the post-reboot capture, matching the prepared baseline content implied by its recorded hashes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: /srv/inventory (and its contents) were reassigned to inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750/640 permissions, verified by live positive (owner, group member) and negative (outsider, nobody) access tests both before and after a full node1 reboot, and the original file contents were unchanged throughout. The executor also independently ran the provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: a pre-restart boot_id/healthy baseline, an acknowledged systemctl reboot, connection loss during the restart window, a different post-restart boot_id, and full recovery of ownership, permissions, and data — all consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (7223d5b7... -> 34604691...).
limitations: No cryptographic hash comparison was performed by the executor against the prepared baseline hashes; content equality was verified only by visual/textual match across captured cat outputs.
The restart was not strictly required by the public task contract, so its evidence is supplemental and does not affect the task-outcome scoring, only overall evidence quality.

operational_hygiene.summary: The only state-changing actions beyond the required chown/chmod and inventorysvc/inventory-readers creation were two temporary test accounts (reader-tester, outsider-tester) created to directly verify the group-read/other-deny requirement — a legitimate verification purpose. Their removal (cmd-068413e8dd064a71, cmd-f72242f73eeb400e) initially failed because lingering systemd --user sessions held the uids busy; a third attempt with loginctl terminate-user and kill -9 (cmd-02fd782ef6a24360) succeeded, confirmed by the empty getent lookup at the end of that command. No residue of the test accounts remains in later observations (post-reboot getent only lists inventorysvc/inventory-readers). No unrelated services, packages, or exposure were touched; failed-services, listening-sockets, and package-health are unchanged apart from the expected sshd pid change from the reboot. The reboot itself, while not strictly required by the task, was bounded, acknowledged, and fully recovered.
